articles.title: Have the clinical signs of a serious type of blood cancer changed?
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers report that newer multiple myeloma treatments may require clinicians to revise which clinical criteria identify patients with poorer survival prospects. The study was published online in Cancer.

articles.title: New topology-based biomarkers may improve breast cancer prediction
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers developed a computational approach that converts tissue architecture patterns seen by pathologists into quantitative measures. The topology-based biomarkers may help improve breast cancer outcome prediction and guide therapy decisions, but the report describes a research advance rather than routine clinical use.

articles.title: Scientists develop DNA-delivered immunotherapy that targets ovarian cancer more effectively
articles.summary_3_sentences: Wistar scientists developed a DNA-delivered bispecific T cell engager aimed at ovarian cancer. The treatment was effective in preclinical studies, highlighting a potential strategy for solid tumors while remaining at an early research stage.

articles.title: AI detection not automatically better for colorectal cancer screening in Lynch syndrome, study shows
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers tested whether artificial intelligence improves detection of precancerous lesions during colonoscopy in people with Lynch syndrome. In specialized centers, AI did not provide a significant added benefit, according to findings published in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology.

articles.title: Cancer survivors and providers differ in views on medical cannabis, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study examined how cancer survivors and health care providers view medical cannabis for symptoms such as pain, nausea, and anxiety. The report notes gaps in knowledge and comfort around discussing cannabis despite widespread legalization and growing use.

articles.title: Cutting-edge drug shows promise for patients with NRAS-driven melanoma
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Huntsman Cancer Institute team reports that a pathway-targeted therapy may benefit patients with NRAS-driven melanoma. The article frames the approach as a potential option for an unmet need in advanced disease.

articles.title: LIG1 loss exposes a therapeutic vulnerability in triple-negative breast cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that loss of one copy of LIG1 in TP53-mutated triple-negative breast cancer can contribute to chemotherapy resistance. They identified mechanisms of platinum resistance and used drug combinations to reduce tumor growth in animal models, suggesting LIG1 status could help stratify patients in trials.

articles.title: This sugar-coated therapy boosted survival against deadly brain cancer by 50% in mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers used sugar-coated nanoparticles to deliver genetic instructions intended to restore a tumor-suppressing protein in glioblastoma cells. In mouse studies, the experimental therapy increased median survival by 50% and reduced tumors without noted organ damage, but it remains preclinical.

articles.title: This pet gecko could help scientists unlock the secrets of cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified a leopard gecko that naturally develops aggressive tumors as a possible model for cancer research. Its tumors share key genetic changes with human cancers, offering a way to study tumor development in a naturally occurring animal model.

articles.title: Scientists finally solved how a common gut bacterium triggers colon cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers described how a bacterial toxin linked to colorectal cancer binds claudin-4 and damages the colon's protective barrier. They designed a decoy protein that blocked the toxin in mice, suggesting a possible route for preventing inflammation and colon tumors in future research.

articles.title: Eating chili peppers may raise the risk of one deadly cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: A major review found an association between the highest chili pepper consumption and increased esophageal cancer risk. The evidence was less clear for stomach and colorectal cancers, and the researchers emphasized that the findings do not prove causation.

articles.title: Why are healthy young non-smokers developing lung cancer?
articles.summary_3_sentences: A preliminary study reported higher lung cancer rates among young non-smokers with healthier diets, raising questions about possible pesticide exposure from conventionally grown produce. Researchers stressed that the findings are unexpected and require further study before conclusions can be drawn.

articles.title: Study identifies chrononutrition as a viable approach for postpartum weight loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that postpartum weight-loss approaches based on meal timing may be more promising when they fit a mother's existing routine. The study highlighted barriers to chrononutrition and noted the importance of preserving family evening meals.

articles.title: Excessive weight gain during pregnancy increases risk of serious complications, no matter your weight
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of more than 1 million women linked excessive pregnancy weight gain with higher risk of serious complications across starting weight categories. The reported increased risk ranged from 16% to 33%, with the highest risk among women who were underweight before pregnancy.

articles.title: Coffee may help the body fight stress and aging through a hidden cellular switch
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists reported that compounds in coffee may activate NR4A1, a receptor linked to cellular protection from stress, inflammation, and damage. The effects disappeared when the receptor was removed, and plant-based compounds such as caffeic acid appeared more active than caffeine itself.

articles.title: Intermittent fasting helped people keep weight off for a year
articles.summary_3_sentences: A 12-week intermittent fasting program was associated with weight-loss benefits that remained visible one year later. Participants using an eight-hour eating window maintained more weight loss than those following their usual longer eating schedule, with both early and late windows showing benefit.

articles.title: Popular sugar substitutes linked to faster brain aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: Adults with the highest intake of several artificial sweeteners showed faster declines in memory and thinking, especially those under 60 or with diabetes. Researchers said more studies are needed before concluding that sweeteners cause cognitive decline.

articles.title: Aussie supermarkets failing to help us eat a healthier diet
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research presented at the International Congress on Obesity found that few of the world's 21 largest food retailers are taking major voluntary steps to create healthier food environments. The findings focus on actions affecting children and families.

articles.title: Scientists tested 39 sweeteners and found unexpected gut effects
articles.summary_3_sentences: A laboratory study found that many common sweeteners can directly alter gut bacterial growth. Researchers also identified interactions with medications, caffeine, and flavorings, including a disruptive combination of isosteviol and duloxetine.

articles.title: Mediterranean diet may activate tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported that older adults who more closely followed a Mediterranean diet had higher levels of mitochondrial microproteins humanin and SHMOOSE. These proteins have been linked to heart and brain protection, and the findings may inform future personalized nutrition research.

articles.title: Lost Sleep Leads to Weight Gain
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that insufficient sleep may contribute to weight gain and metabolic risk. It also notes possible links to obesity, heart disease, and diabetes.

articles.title: Gut Microbes Work as a Vitamin A Delivery System
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that some gut bacteria may act as a delivery system for vitamin A. The work adds to evidence that gut microbes can influence nutrient handling and broader health-related functions.

articles.title: Popular weight-loss drugs Ozempic and Wegovy may slow biological aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, slowed biological aging markers in adults with HIV. The finding is described as early clinical evidence, and larger studies are needed before concluding that the drug slows aging broadly.

articles.title: Chewing bubble gum after beetroot may help lower blood pressure
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found that chewing sugary gum after eating nitrate-rich vegetables or drinking beetroot juice increased production of beneficial nitrite. The change was linked to a temporary blood pressure drop, though researchers hope to find healthier ways to enhance dietary nitrate effects without added sugar.

articles.title: Losing just 80 minutes of sleep a night could make you gain weight
articles.summary_3_sentences: Participants who slept about 80 minutes less each night for six weeks gained weight and spent more time inactive. Researchers warned that mild but sustained sleep loss could have larger health consequences over time.

articles.title: During Aging, Cells Develop a Preference for Short Genes
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported that aging cells show a shift in gene transcription toward shorter genes. The finding points to a possible change in RNA polymerase II activity and gene expression patterns during cellular aging.

articles.title: Dementia patients gain peace, connection from live concert series
articles.summary_3_sentences: A live concert series is described as helping people with dementia experience peace and social connection. The article frames the program in the context of growing evidence that lifelong learning and engagement may support cognitive health.

articles.title: What does resilience show about healthy aging after trauma?
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of wartime trauma among Vietnamese Americans received additional funding to examine how trauma affects aging and brain health. The project aims to investigate resilience and healthy aging after traumatic experiences.

articles.title: Heavy TV watching associated with smaller brain structures, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers report an association between heavy television watching and smaller brain structures. The article does not establish that TV watching causes brain changes, but it suggests the relationship may merit attention.

articles.title: Watching live sports together boosts oxytocin and synchronizes heartbeats, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found that watching live sports with others boosted oxytocin and synchronized heartbeats. The findings are presented in the context of social bonding and psychological well-being.

articles.title: Researchers test video game as anxiety treatment for teens
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers are testing a video game-based approach as a potential anxiety treatment for teenagers. The article notes that teen anxiety can affect school, friendships, and daily activities.

articles.title: The mysterious hum heard around the world may finally have an explanation
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers investigated whether people who hear the global phenomenon known as The Hum have exceptional low-frequency hearing or measurable sounds produced in their ears. Those explanations did not fit most participants, and the study suggests many cases may involve low-frequency tinnitus perceived as external.

articles.title: New study sheds light on how Epstein-Barr virus may contribute to multiple sclerosis
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study explored how Epstein-Barr virus may contribute to multiple sclerosis, a chronic autoimmune disease of the central nervous system. The article notes the strong epidemiological link between EBV infection and later MS risk.

articles.title: How brain remodeling during adolescence shapes memory
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a biological process in mice that may help explain how memory circuits mature during adolescent brain development. The work offers mechanistic insight but is based on animal research.

articles.title: Cut the number of choices you make each day. Your brain will thank you Jeans that fit perfectly. The ideal Netflix show for a Tuesday night. Your one and only soulmate. Modern life promises that with enough options, you will happily find the best of everything.
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses the cognitive burden of making many everyday choices. It suggests that reducing decision load may benefit the brain, though no detailed study findings were provided in the record.

articles.title: Your fingers may hold a secret of human brain evolution
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of 225 newborns found that boys with finger-length patterns linked to higher prenatal estrogen exposure tended to have larger head circumferences. The same association was not seen in girls, and the findings are presented as evidence relevant to hypotheses about human brain evolution.

articles.title: THC/CBD Reduces Agitation in Late-Stage Dementia
articles.summary_3_sentences: A combination of THC and CBD significantly reduced agitation in people with late-stage dementia. The record provides limited detail on the study design or safety findings.

articles.title: The hidden skeleton "gatekeeper" inside brain cells could help fight Alzheimer's
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that a microscopic structural network inside neurons helps control what brain cells absorb. When the structure weakens, neurons rapidly take in proteins associated with Alzheimer's disease, suggesting a possible protective target for future studies.

articles.title: Dementia Prevention Strategies Should Be Country-Specific
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that dementia risk factors vary widely across countries. It argues that prevention strategies may need to be tailored rather than based on a single global approach.

articles.title: Where you live could shape your dementia risk, massive study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers analyzing data from more than 214,000 people found that dementia risk factors differ substantially by country. The study also identified some consistent patterns that could inform targeted public health prevention efforts.

articles.title: Common constipation drug may help clear depression brain fog
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a small clinical trial, people with a history of depression who took prucalopride for about a week performed better on tests of memory, attention, and thinking speed than those receiving placebo. The drug targets a serotonin receptor in the gut and brain, and no significant side effects were reported in the record.

articles.title: Scientists discovered the brain doesn't make decisions the way we thought
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study suggests that decision-making begins earlier in the brain than previously thought, with primary sensory regions influenced by rapid feedback from higher brain areas. The findings support a more dynamic model of brain processing and may inform future biologically inspired AI systems.

articles.title: Scientists discover how the brain rewires itself to truly multitask
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that extensive training can reorganize the brain so learned tasks rely less on the prefrontal cortex and more on specialized circuits. This may free cognitive resources and improve performance on another task at the same time.

articles.title: New Alzheimer's drug repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
articles.summary_3_sentences: A drug originally developed for spinal cord injury reduced DNA damage and inflammation in mouse models of Alzheimer's disease. The compound, KCL-286, has reportedly passed an initial human safety trial, but the Alzheimer's findings remain preclinical.

articles.title: Alzheimer's tau protein has a surprising secret role in memory
articles.summary_3_sentences: A mouse study found that tau helps convert new experiences into lasting memories by organizing memory-storing cells. The findings also suggest abnormal tau may disrupt both formation and recall of memories in Alzheimer's disease.

topic_groups.topic: Infectious Disease, Microbiome and Public Health

articles.title: Federal housing assistance may protect young children from lead exposure
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study in Environmental Epidemiology found that federal housing assistance may help reduce lead exposure among young children. The report highlights housing policy as a possible protective factor for environmental health.

articles.title: To trial or not to trial: Veteran vaccine advisers say vaccine clinical trials alone don't tell whole story
articles.summary_3_sentences: Two experienced U.S. vaccine policy advisers argue that vaccine effectiveness assessments should include well-designed observational studies as well as clinical trials. Their position is that trials alone may not capture how vaccines perform year to year.

articles.title: Q&A: Cyclospora outbreak
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article explains a U.S. cyclosporiasis outbreak linked to concern over lettuce and leafy greens. It notes that the gastrointestinal illness can cause severe watery diarrhea.

articles.title: Warm nights linked to ill premature babies in NICUs
articles.summary_3_sentences: Doctors in Hanover studied external factors affecting infection risk among premature infants in neonatal intensive care units. They concluded that climatic conditions, including warm nights, influence the risk of potentially pathogenic bacterial infections.

articles.title: Designing better climate research starts with understanding human emotions
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses how emotional reactions to climate-related images such as wildfires, floods, and starving wildlife may shape climate research and communication. It frames human emotion as an important factor in designing better climate research.

articles.title: First death reported in Legionnaires' disease outbreak in New York City
articles.summary_3_sentences: New York City health officials reported the first death in a Legionnaires' disease outbreak that had sickened dozens of people. The article describes an active public health outbreak investigation.

articles.title: A Working Antibacterial Resistance Gene is Found in Nature
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a functional antibacterial resistance gene in nature. The finding suggests that resistance genes can exist naturally and underscores the need for strategies against antibiotic-resistant infections.

articles.title: More than 400 sick as CDC searches for the source of a mystery outbreak
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Cyclospora outbreak sickened more than 400 people in four states while investigators searched for the contaminated food source. The CDC warned that the true number of cases is likely higher and advised symptomatic people to seek medical care.

articles.title: Tiny plastics in drinking water may be making dangerous bacteria stronger
articles.summary_3_sentences: New research suggests nanoplastics in drinking water can strengthen biofilms formed by harmful bacteria in water systems. These tougher biofilms may resist disinfectants more effectively, potentially increasing public health risks.

articles.title: Scientists finally solved why some frogs survive a deadly fungus
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that some frogs survive a deadly fungal disease by developing strong immune defenses while still tadpoles. The study also identified many previously unknown antimicrobial peptides that could inspire future anti-infective research.

topic_groups.topic: Cardiovascular, Kidney and Chronic Disease Care

articles.title: Study shows where women live can shape heart health for decades
articles.summary_3_sentences: A long-term study found that women in disadvantaged neighborhoods had worse heart health and faster declines approaching menopause. The findings suggest neighborhood conditions may shape cardiovascular health over decades.

articles.title: A sales tax on doctor visits and medicine?
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses concerns in Missouri about applying sales tax to doctor visits and medicines. It highlights affordability worries for people managing chronic illnesses and multiple medications.

articles.title: Common antidepressant may ease long COVID's crushing fatigue
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a randomized clinical trial of 399 adults, fluvoxamine reduced fatigue and improved quality of life compared with placebo in people with long COVID. The report describes it as one of the first medications to show meaningful benefit for this symptom, while further confirmation would still be important.

articles.title: Serotonin Linked to Heart Valve Disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that some individuals may have increased risk of heart valve disease progression related to SSRIs. Details are limited, but the record points to a possible serotonin-linked valve disease concern.

articles.title: Cannabis-Infused Tea Boosts Happiness and Sleep
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes a study examining how cannabis-infused tea may influence sleep quality and overall quality of life. The record provides limited details, but reports potential effects on happiness and sleep.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden heart valve risk linked to gum disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that bacteria associated with gum disease may contribute to calcific aortic valve stenosis by promoting inflammation and calcium buildup. The findings are early and suggest oral health may be relevant to heart valve disease risk.

articles.title: This drug could help millions keep their kidneys working longer
articles.summary_3_sentences: An international study found that finerenone slowed kidney function decline and reduced serious kidney and cardiovascular complications in people with chronic kidney disease without diabetes. The results suggest a potential treatment option for many CKD patients who have limited choices.

topic_groups.topic: Ophthalmology, Regeneration, Skin and Musculoskeletal Science

articles.title: Researchers discover the eye's hidden cleanup system
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers described a previously hidden cleanup system in the eye. The finding may be relevant to conditions such as glaucoma and age-related macular degeneration, where fluid, waste, and inflammatory debris build up in the back of the eye.

articles.title: When healing injuries, timing of regenerative cues matters
articles.summary_3_sentences: University of Oregon research suggests that the timing of regenerative cues is critical during injury healing. The work reinforces the importance of delivering signals at the right time as well as to the right place.

articles.title: Discovery could lead to drug therapy for hypopigmentation conditions
articles.summary_3_sentences: A preclinical study found that ampyrone, an NSAID-related compound, can safely boost melanin production in human skin. The discovery could support development of ampyrone-derived therapies for hypopigmentation disorders.

articles.title: Yale scientists found a hidden network inside the eye
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers discovered an unexpected retinal communication network that allows separate visual pathways to cooperate. A newly identified coordinating cell may help the eye detect faint details.

articles.title: Scientists discover why peach fuzz can suddenly make you itch
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified a network of fine hairs and specialized nerve cells that appears to sense mechanical itch. Because humans show signs of a similar pathway, the work could inform future treatments for chronic itch conditions such as eczema.

articles.title: This ultrasound treatment may help stop arthritis before it starts
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that continuous low-intensity ultrasound encouraged macrophages to shift from an inflammatory state toward a tissue-repair state. The non-invasive approach could eventually help injured joints heal, but the record describes early research rather than a proven arthritis prevention treatment.

topic_groups.topic: General Science, Evolution and Research Methods

articles.title: Koalas nearly went extinct before humans arrived, DNA study reveals
articles.summary_3_sentences: A DNA study found that koalas underwent a major population collapse about 100,000 years ago, before humans arrived in Australia. By estimating the koala mutation rate and analyzing hundreds of genomes, researchers traced living koalas to a small group that survived extreme climate shifts.

articles.title: Beyond the bead: rethinking small-scale protein purification
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses new approaches to small-scale protein purification used in research and process development. The methods aim to improve efficiency, scalability, and purification workflow design.

articles.title: Going to museums, movies, and theater may help your body stay younger
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that older adults who regularly participated in cultural activities had bodies that functioned like those of people about three years younger. The authors suggested social ties, mental health, and healthier habits may help explain the association, but causality is not established.

articles.title: Deep-sea life has a secret food source scientists never expected
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists found that extreme deep-sea pressure can squeeze nutrients from sinking organic particles, creating an unexpected food source for ocean microbes. The discovery may change understanding of deep-ocean ecosystems and carbon storage.
